your_book:
Friday was a bruising session for Jaleel's book, with two holdings delivering sharp single-session drops that overshadowed the few bright spots. Lululemon (LULU) cratered 17.4% — its stock hitting an 8-year low — as the market absorbed what appears to be an earnings or guidance event on top of an already-flagged risk: five straight quarters of negative Americas comps, tariff-gutted margins, and a stalled China business. The next read on LULU isn't until December 9, so the pain sits with no near-term catalyst for relief. Adobe (ADBE) fell 6.7% despite its risk flag pointing to narrative rather than numbers — AI-disruption fear around Claude Design and a CFO departure continue to weigh; critically, earnings land September 10, just three days away. Boston Scientific (BSX) was a rare bright spot, gaining 1.8% despite carrying an elevated guidance-cut flag. NVDA added 0.84%, helped by Foxconn flagging record August revenue and surging AI demand. The rest of the book was broadly red, with Danaher (−1.6%), AstraZeneca (−1.3%), and Equifax (−6.4%) dragging alongside the broader softness.

Divergence between price and thesis is most glaring in three spots. LULU carries a BUY verdict with a QARP of 71.9 yet sits 21.3% underwater in the book — the thesis requires a turnaround that is moving further away, not closer, with each data point. RKLB is rated AVOID, sits 18% in the red, and still holds a 6.5% weight — the largest misalignment between model conviction and book sizing. BSX is rated STRONG BUY (QARP 77.4) but down 2.5% in cost terms and operating under a slashed growth guide; the model is more constructive than management's own guidance, which is worth stress-testing before the October 28 print.

Watch the ADBE print on September 10 closely — that's the fulcrum event for the coming week. LULU's next scheduled catalyst isn't until December, meaning any thesis re-evaluation has to happen on fundamentals conviction alone, not an upcoming number. With the book's overall unrealized gain sitting at just under 2% and a meaningful number of positions in the red, capital preservation demands honest scrutiny of positions where the model says one thing and price says another.
